title.narrative: Joint Programme for Sustainable Urban Integration of Displaced Populations in Northern Nigeria

description.narrative:
The Action addresses the sustainable local urban integration of internally displaced persons (IDPs), including women and children in Northern Nigeria, focusing on the States of Adamawa, Yobe and Kano metropolitan areas, to also benefit host communities in their diversity. By operationalizing a multi-scale territorial approach that converges with development priorities, policies and strategies of the concerned State governments, the Action aims to provide a framework from which mechanisms and guidelines can be established to replicate durable local urban integration solutions at scale, thus catalysing the mobilization of additional resources and investments. At the regional level, the project aligns with the African Union’s Kampala Convention, which It is the first and only binding regional treaty in the world that specifically addresses the protection and assistance of internally displaced persons (IDPs).The Action contributes to the implementation of Nigeria’s 2021 National Policy on IDPs and the UN Secretary-General Action Agenda on Internal Displacement in Nigeria and is aligned with the institutional approaches for durable solutions of UN-Habitat, IOM and UNHCR. It will explore linkages with the State Action Plans on durable solutions recently endorsed by Adamawa and Yobe States, and existing coordination structures at the State and Local Government Area (LGA) levels.
The Action is directed at: (i) strengthening the capacity of State and Local Government Areas (LGAs) authorities, displaced and host communities in harnessing rapid urban growth as a solution to displacement through local integration; (ii) supporting the inclusion of displaced populations in state development plans and local urban plans that respond to the needs of women and children; (iii) facilitating access to secured land and adequate housing for marginalized groups, including displaced women and children, including access to basic and social services, and strengthening the protection environment, especially for women and children; and (iv) enhancing social cohesion between displaced and host populations by supporting community-led initiatives meant to increase livelihood and generate income for all.
At the State level, the Action aims to strengthen institutional capacity to establish mechanisms for improving policies, strategies and plans for local urban integration, ensuring that they respond to the needs of the impacted communities in their diversity, involving collaboration among Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), to enable sustainability, replication and scaling-up of the proposed approach.
At the LGA level, it focuses on strengthening urban planning and management capacities with the support of the state governments, especially on issues related to land management.
At the community level, the Action will deliver development solutions that promote social cohesion, stimulate local economic development (LED) and strengthen the delivery of protection services, especially for the most marginalized, including access to secure land tenure, to facilitate the integration of displaced populations into the socio-economic fabric of their host communities. It will enhance access to basic and social services in line with local priorities determined through a participatory approach, by involving both displaced and host communities, ensuring that all members of the communities can effectively participate, including women, children, youth and older persons. It will also establish sustainable mechanisms to promote self-help housing for all.
The Overall Objective of this Action is to enable durable solutions through local integration in urban and urbanising areas by adopting a multi-scale, integrated, gender-responsive and area-based territorial approach for displaced communities, host communities and local authorities in the States of Adamawa, Yobe and Kano metropolitan area with a specific focus on women and children, and fostering conditions for sustainability, replication and scaling-up.
The action’s Overall Objective is underpinned by one Specific Objective (in line with the second Specific Objective of the EU Action Document for Protection, Assistance and Durable Solutions for Populations Displaced by Conflict in Sub-Saharan Africa), which is to provide durable solutions for forcibly displaced populations, particularly women and children, in States where policy frameworks are in place.
The Overall Expected Result of this Action is that the living conditions of forcibly displaced populations and host communities, including women and children, in Adamawa State, Yobe State, and Kano metropolitan areas have been significantly enhanced thanks to a sustainable local urban integration approach that is replicable and can be scaled up.
